title: Have to, might, some, any and linking words

blurb.en: Use have to, might, some, any, linking words and adverbs to build good sentences.
blurb.vi: Dùng have to, might, some, any, từ nối và trạng từ để viết câu hay.

have to.def: It is necessary, or it is a rule. You must do it.
have to.ex: You *have to* wear a seat belt in the car.

had to.def: It was necessary in the past. It was a rule then.
had to.ex: Yesterday the lift was broken, so we *had to* use the stairs.

might.def: Maybe it will happen, but we are not sure.
might.ex: Take a jumper. It *might* be cold on the mountain.

could.def: It is possible. We use it to give an idea.
could.ex: We're bored. We *could* make a paper boat!

a few.def: A small number of things you can count.
a few.ex: There are *a few* strawberries in the bowl.

a little.def: A small amount of something you cannot count, like water or rice.
a little.ex: Can I have *a little* water, please?

many.def: A lot of things you can count. We often use it in questions.
many.ex: How *many* stars can you see tonight?

much.def: A lot of something you cannot count. We use it in questions and with 'not'.
much.ex: We haven't got *much* time, so please hurry.

every.def: All the people or things in a group, one by one.
every.ex: *Every* child in our class has a name badge.

something.def: A thing, but we do not say which one.
something.ex: Grandpa has got *something* for you in his bag.

nothing.ex: My piggy bank is empty. There's *nothing* in it.

before.ex: Look left and right *before* you cross the road.

while.def: At the same time as another action.
while.ex: I listened to music *while* I was drawing.

more carefully.def: In a slower and safer way than another person or another time.
more carefully.ex: Dad cut the wood *more carefully* than me.

title.en: Have to, had to, might and could
title.vi: Have to, had to, might và could

scenes.head: A note from the climbing club
scenes.html:
Climbing Club: Saturday trip
On Saturday we are going to the big climbing wall in the city. You *have to* wear a helmet. You *don't have to* bring lunch: we will buy pizza there. The bus *might* be late, so please wait inside the club. It *may* be cold, so you *could* bring a jumper. Last time we *had to* wait for an hour!

steps.en: *have to* = it is a rule. You must do it. *don't have to* = it is not necessary. You can choose.
steps.vi: *have to* = đây là quy định, con phải làm. *don't have to* = không cần thiết, con có thể tự chọn.

steps.en: *had to* is the past of *have to*. Last time we *had to* wait.
steps.vi: *had to* là quá khứ của *have to*. Lần trước chúng ta đã phải chờ.

steps.en: *might* and *may* = maybe. We are not sure. The bus *might* be late.
steps.vi: *might* và *may* = có lẽ. Chúng ta không chắc chắn. Xe buýt có lẽ sẽ đến muộn.

steps.en: *could* = a possible idea. You *could* bring a jumper.
steps.vi: *could* = một ý kiến có thể làm. Con có thể mang theo áo len.

scenes.head: Hana and Grandpa in the kitchen
scenes.html:
Hana: Let's make mango smoothies! Have we got *any* mangoes?
Grandpa: Yes, we've got *a few* mangoes. Not *many*.
Hana: Is there *any* yoghurt?
Grandpa: There's *a little* yoghurt in the fridge. There's *nothing* else in there!
Hana: Do we need *something* sweet?
Grandpa: Yes. *Every* smoothie needs *some* honey. But not *much*!

steps.en: *a few* and *many* go with things we can count: mangoes, cups, stars.
steps.vi: *a few* và *many* đi với những thứ đếm được: quả xoài, cái cốc, ngôi sao.

steps.en: *a little* and *much* go with things we cannot count: yoghurt, honey, rice.
steps.vi: *a little* và *much* đi với những thứ không đếm được: sữa chua, mật ong, gạo.
Câu khẳng định: *some*, *something*. Câu hỏi và câu phủ định: *any*, *anything*.
*nothing* = không có gì. *Every* + danh từ số ít: *every* smoothie.

title.en: Linking words and how we do things
title.vi: Từ nối và cách chúng ta làm việc

scenes.head: Rhys writes about the bird house
scenes.html: Last Sunday Dad and I made a bird house. *Before* we started, we read the plan. Dad cut the wood *while* I painted the roof. *Then* we put it together. Dad measured *more carefully* than me! *After* we finished, we put it in our tree. *When* the first bird came, I shouted. My sister shouted *the loudest*! The bird flew away *faster* than a rocket.

steps.en: *before*, *after*, *then* and *when* tell us the order of things.
steps.vi: *before*, *after*, *then* và *when* cho biết thứ tự các việc.

steps.en: *while* = at the same time. Dad cut the wood *while* I painted.
steps.vi: *while* = cùng lúc. Bố cắt gỗ trong khi tớ sơn.

steps.en: Short adverbs: fast, *faster*, the fastest. Long adverbs: carefully, *more carefully*, the most carefully.
steps.vi: Trạng từ ngắn: fast, *faster*, the fastest. Trạng từ dài: carefully, *more carefully*, the most carefully.

steps.en: Use *than* to compare two. Use *the* ...*est* or *the most* for the top one.
steps.vi: Dùng *than* để so sánh hai người. Dùng *the* ...*est* hoặc *the most* cho người nhất.

end.en: Now try the grammar tools on your own!
end.vi: Bây giờ con hãy tự dùng các công cụ ngữ pháp nhé!

challenge.result: You spotted have to, might, quantity words, some, any, linking words and adverbs!

v.q: Which sentence means 'maybe'?
opts: We had to wait an hour.
whys: 'have to' is a rule, not a maybe.
'had to' is a rule in the past, not a maybe.
v.hint: Is it a rule, or are we guessing?
v.worked: 'might' = maybe: 'The bus might be late'.

v.q: Which sentence is about a rule in the past?
opts: We had to wear a helmet.
whys: 'might' means maybe, not a rule.
'could' gives an idea, not a rule.
v.hint: Look for the past form of 'have to'.
v.worked: 'had to' is the past of 'have to': 'We had to wear a helmet'.

v.q: Which one is correct?
whys: 'a little' goes with things we cannot count, like yoghurt.
'much' goes with things we cannot count, like honey.
v.hint: Can you count mangoes?
v.worked: We can count mangoes, so we say 'a few mangoes'.

v.q: Which one is correct?
whys: 'a few' goes with things we can count, like cups.
'many' goes with things we can count, like stars.
v.hint: Can you count honey?
v.worked: We cannot count honey, so we say 'a little honey'.

v.q: My piggy bank is empty. There's ________ in it.
whys: The piggy bank is empty, so there isn't a thing in it.
We don't use 'anything' after 'There's'. We use it after 'There isn't'.
v.hint: Is the piggy bank full or empty? Then check the word after 'There's'.
v.worked: Empty piggy bank = 'There's nothing in it'.

v.q: There isn't ________ in my bag.
whys: 'isn't' and 'nothing' together make two 'no' words.
After 'isn't' we use 'anything', not 'something'.
v.hint: Look for 'not' in the sentence.
v.worked: 'not' sentence + any: 'There isn't anything in my bag'.

v.q: Dad cut the wood ________ I painted the roof. We did it at the same time.
whys: 'before' means earlier, but they did it at the same time.
'then' means next, but they did it at the same time.
v.hint: Read the second sentence. When did they do it?
v.worked: At the same time = 'while': 'Dad cut the wood while I painted'.

v.q: Dad measured ________ than me.
whys: Look for 'than'. We need a word that compares two people.
'most carefully' is for the top one of a group, not two people.
v.hint: Look for the word 'than'.
v.worked: 'than' compares two people: 'more carefully than me'.

blurb.en: Practise one grammar tool at a time: have to, quantity words, some and any, linking words.
blurb.vi: Luyện từng công cụ ngữ pháp: have to, từ chỉ số lượng, some và any, từ nối.

title.en: Have to, had to, might and could
title.vi: Have to, had to, might và could

v.q: It's a rule. You ________ wear a seat belt in the car.
whys: 'might' means maybe, but this is a rule.
'could' gives an idea, but this is a rule.
v.hint: Is it a rule or a maybe?
v.worked: A rule uses 'have to': 'You have to wear a seat belt'.

v.q: Grandma's cat isn't in the garden. It ________ be under the bed.
whys: 'has to' is for rules. We are only guessing where the cat is.
'had to' is a rule in the past. We are guessing about now.
v.hint: Do we know where the cat is, or are we guessing?
v.worked: We are not sure, so: 'It might be under the bed'.

v.q: Write the missing word.
lines: Yesterday the lift was broken. We {0} to walk up the stairs.
v.hint: 'Yesterday' is the past. Which past word goes before 'to'?
v.worked: A rule in the past: 'We had to walk up the stairs'.

v.q: Write the missing word.
lines: It's Saturday! I don't {0} to get up early.
v.hint: It is not necessary on Saturday. Which word goes in 'don't ... to'?
v.worked: Not necessary: 'I don't have to get up early' ('don't need to' is also correct).

v.q: We're bored. We ________ play a board game!
whys: 'had to' is a rule in the past, but this is an idea for now.
'have to' is a rule, but this is just a fun idea.
v.hint: Is it a rule, or an idea?
v.worked: To give an idea we use 'could': 'We could play a board game!'

v.q: Take your coat. It ________ be cold on the mountain.
whys: 'has to' is for rules. Nobody makes a rule about the weather.
'had to' is the past, but the trip is in the future.
v.hint: Are we sure about the weather?
v.worked: We are not sure, so: 'It may be cold'.

title.vi: Từ chỉ số lượng, some và any

v.q: There are ________ biscuits in the tin. Not many.
whys: 'a little' goes with things we cannot count, like sugar.
'much' goes with things we cannot count, like water.
v.hint: Can you count biscuits?
v.worked: We can count biscuits, so: 'a few biscuits'.

v.q: Can I have ________ water, please? Just half a glass.
whys: 'a few' goes with things we can count, like cups.
'many' goes with things we can count, like glasses.
v.hint: Can you count water?
v.worked: We cannot count water, so: 'a little water'.

v.q: We haven't got ________ pets.
whys: After 'haven't' we use 'any', not 'some'.
'haven't' and 'nothing' together make two 'no' words.
v.hint: Look for 'not' in the sentence.
v.worked: 'not' sentence + any: 'We haven't got any pets'.

v.q: I'm hungry. I want ________ to eat.
whys: 'anything' goes in questions and 'not' sentences. This is a yes sentence.
'nothing' means not one thing, but the speaker is hungry.
v.hint: Is this a yes sentence, a 'not' sentence or a question?
v.worked: A yes sentence uses 'something': 'I want something to eat'.

v.q: Write the missing word.
lines: My piggy bank is empty. There's {0} in it.
v.hint: Read the first sentence. Is there a thing in the piggy bank?
v.worked: Empty = not one thing: 'There's nothing in it'.

v.q: Write the missing word.
lines: We all wear a blue hat. {0} child in our class has one.
v.hint: Look at 'child' and 'has': it is one child. Which word means all of them, one by one?
v.worked: We all wear one, so: '*Every* child has one' (or '*Each* child').

v.q: Brush your teeth ________ you go to bed.
whys: 'after' would mean you go to bed first, then brush.
'while' means at the same time, but you brush first, then sleep.
v.hint: Which do you do first?
v.worked: First brush, then bed: 'Brush your teeth before you go to bed'.

v.q: I sang a song ________ I was washing the dishes.
whys: With 'was ...ing' the two things happen at the same time, so 'before' doesn't fit.
'then' means next, but the singing and washing were at the same time.
v.hint: Look at 'was washing'. Did the two things happen at the same time?
v.worked: At the same time = 'while': 'I sang while I was washing'.

v.q: Thu speaks ________ than her brother. He is very quiet.
whys: 'loudly' does not compare two people. Look for 'than'.
'most loudly' is for the top one of a group, not two people.
v.hint: Look for the word 'than'.
v.worked: 'than' compares two people: 'more loudly than her brother'.

v.q: Khoa can swim ________ of all the children in his class.
whys: 'faster' compares two people, but here it is 'of all the children'.
'fast' doesn't compare. Look for 'of all'.
v.hint: Look for 'of all'. Is he the top one?
v.worked: 'of all' = the top one: 'the fastest'.

v.q: Write the missing word.
lines: First we made the dough. {0} we put it in the oven.
v.hint: Which linking word starts the second step?
v.worked: Step 1, then step 2: '*Then* we put it in the oven' ('Next' or 'After that' is also correct).

v.q: Write the missing word.
lines: Max writes neatly, but Ella writes {0} neatly than Max. Her letters are perfect!
v.hint: 'neatly' is a long adverb. Look for 'than'.
v.worked: Long adverb + than: 'more neatly than Max'.

blurb.en: Exam practice: choose the right word, the best reply and the words for a story.
blurb.vi: Luyện thi: chọn từ đúng, câu trả lời phù hợp nhất và từ cho bài kể chuyện.

v.q: It's a club rule. We ________ put the balls away after training.
whys: 'might' means maybe, but putting the balls away is a club rule.
'may' means maybe, but putting the balls away is a club rule.
v.hint: Read the first sentence. Is it a rule, or a maybe?
v.worked: A club rule uses 'have to': 'we have to put the balls away'.

v.q: I'm not sure, but Arjun ________ come to the party.
whys: 'has to' is a rule, but the speaker is not sure.
'had to' is a rule in the past, and the party is in the future.
v.hint: Read the start: 'I'm not sure'.
v.worked: Not sure = maybe: 'Arjun might come to the party'.

v.q: We haven't got ________ time, so please be quick.
whys: 'many' goes with things we can count, like minutes. 'time' is not counted here.
'a few' goes with things we can count, and it doesn't fit after 'haven't got'.
v.hint: Can you count 'time' in this sentence?
v.worked: 'time' is uncountable here, and the sentence has 'not': 'much time'.

v.q: Our teacher showed us ________ photos of the planets.
whys: 'a little' goes with things we cannot count, like juice.
'much' goes with things we cannot count, like rice.
v.hint: Can you count photos?
v.worked: We can count photos, so: 'a few photos'.

v.q: I looked in my bag, but I didn't find ________.
whys: After 'didn't' we use 'anything', not 'something'.
'didn't' and 'nothing' together make two 'no' words.
v.hint: Look for 'not' in the sentence.
v.worked: 'not' sentence + any: 'I didn't find anything'.

v.q: Listen! I can hear ________ in the kitchen.
whys: 'anything' goes in questions and 'not' sentences. This is a yes sentence.
The speaker says 'Listen!', so there is a sound. 'nothing' doesn't fit.
v.hint: Is it a yes sentence, a 'not' sentence or a question?
v.worked: A yes sentence uses 'something': 'I can hear something'.

title.vi: Phần 2: chọn câu trả lời phù hợp nhất

v.q: "Are you coming to the beach with us tomorrow?" Choose the best reply.
opts: I might. I'll ask my mum.
I had to. It was fun.
whys: 'had to' and 'was' are the past, but the question is about tomorrow.
'went yesterday' is the past, but the question is about tomorrow.
v.hint: Is the question about the past or the future?
v.worked: Tomorrow is the future, and the speaker isn't sure yet: 'I might. I'll ask my mum.'

v.q: "Why can't you play football after school today?" Choose the best reply.
opts: I have to visit my grandma.
I had to visit her yesterday.
whys: This is about yesterday, but the question is about today.
This says when you might play, not why you can't play today.
v.hint: The question starts with 'Why'. Find a reason for today.
v.worked: A reason for today: 'I have to visit my grandma'.

v.q: "Is there any juice for me?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Yes, there's a little in the fridge.
Yes, there are a few in the fridge.
No, but there are many in the fridge.
whys: 'a few' and 'are' go with things we can count, but juice is not counted.
'many' goes with things we can count, and 'No' and 'many' don't agree.
v.hint: Can you count juice?
v.worked: Juice is uncountable: 'there's a little in the fridge'.

v.q: "What's in that big box, Duc?" Choose the best reply.
whys: This answers a yes/no question, but the question starts with 'What'.
This says what you haven't got, not what is in the box.
v.hint: The question starts with 'What'. Does a yes or no answer fit?
v.worked: 'What's in the box?' 'Nothing. It's empty!' tells us what is in it.

v.q: "When can I watch TV, Mum?" Choose the best reply.
whys: This is about last night, but the question asks when you can watch now.
'Because' gives a reason, but the question asks 'When'.
v.hint: The question starts with 'When'. Which reply gives a time?
v.worked: 'When?' needs a time: 'After you tidy your room'.

v.q: "Your drawing is beautiful! How did you make it so neat?" Choose the best reply.
opts: I drew more slowly this time.
I drew it at home yesterday.
whys: This says when, not how you made it neat.
This says what you like, not how you made it neat.
v.hint: The question asks 'How'. Which reply says how you did it?
v.worked: 'How?' needs a way of doing it: 'I drew more slowly this time'.

title.vi: Phần 4: bài kể chuyện có chỗ trống

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: 'might' means maybe, but the next sentence says it was a rule.
'could' means it was possible, but the next sentence says it was a rule.
v.hint: Read the sentence after the gap.
v.worked: 'It was our teacher's rule', so: 'Everyone had to wear gloves'.

stim.head: A story by Mia
stim.html:
Clean-up Day in Our Street
Last Saturday my class helped to clean our street. Everyone (1) ________ wear gloves. It was our teacher's rule.
We found a lot of rubbish. There were (2) ________ plastic bottles under the trees. I picked up twenty!
(3) ________ we finished, we ate ice lollies together. We were hot and tired from all the work.
Now our street looks clean and beautiful. I'm proud of my class.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: 'After' would mean they put on their boots at the end of the walk.
'While' means at the same time, but they got ready first.
v.hint: When do you put on boots and fill bottles: at the start or at the end?
v.worked: They got ready first: 'Before we started, we put on our boots'.

stim.head: A story by Arjun
stim.html:
Our Walk up the Mountain
Last holiday my uncle and I walked up a small mountain. (1) ________ we started, we put on our boots and filled our bottles.
The path was steep. My uncle's bag was very heavy, so he walked (2) ________ than me. I waited for him at the top.
We were hungry, but we didn't have (3) ________ food left. Luckily, a woman at the top sold us some noodles!
The view was amazing. I could see our whole town.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: 'much' goes with things we cannot count, but we can count bottles.
'a little' goes with things we cannot count, but we can count bottles.
v.hint: Can you count bottles? Read the next sentence too.
v.worked: Bottles are countable and there were a lot: 'many plastic bottles'.

stim.head: A story by Mia
stim.html:
Clean-up Day in Our Street
Last Saturday my class helped to clean our street. Everyone (1) ________ wear gloves. It was our teacher's rule.
We found a lot of rubbish. There were (2) ________ plastic bottles under the trees. I picked up twenty!
(3) ________ we finished, we ate ice lollies together. We were hot and tired from all the work.
Now our street looks clean and beautiful. I'm proud of my class.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: Look for 'than'. We need a word that compares two people.
'most slowly' is for the top one of a group, not two people.
v.hint: Look for 'than' after the gap.
v.worked: 'than me' compares two people: 'he walked more slowly than me'.

stim.head: A story by Arjun
stim.html:
Our Walk up the Mountain
Last holiday my uncle and I walked up a small mountain. (1) ________ we started, we put on our boots and filled our bottles.
The path was steep. My uncle's bag was very heavy, so he walked (2) ________ than me. I waited for him at the top.
We were hungry, but we didn't have (3) ________ food left. Luckily, a woman at the top sold us some noodles!
The view was amazing. I could see our whole town.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (3): choose the word.
whys: They ate the ice lollies at the end, when they were tired from the work.
'While' means at the same time, but they ate after the work.
v.hint: Read the next sentence. Were they tired before or after the work?
v.worked: They were tired from all the work, so: 'After we finished, we ate ice lollies'.

stim.head: A story by Mia
stim.html:
Clean-up Day in Our Street
Last Saturday my class helped to clean our street. Everyone (1) ________ wear gloves. It was our teacher's rule.
We found a lot of rubbish. There were (2) ________ plastic bottles under the trees. I picked up twenty!
(3) ________ we finished, we ate ice lollies together. We were hot and tired from all the work.
Now our street looks clean and beautiful. I'm proud of my class.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (3): choose the word.
whys: 'many' goes with things we can count, but 'food' is not counted.
'a few' goes with things we can count, and 'food' is not counted.
v.hint: Can you count 'food'? Look for 'didn't' too.
v.worked: 'food' is uncountable and the sentence has 'not': 'didn't have much food'.

stim.head: A story by Arjun
stim.html:
Our Walk up the Mountain
Last holiday my uncle and I walked up a small mountain. (1) ________ we started, we put on our boots and filled our bottles.
The path was steep. My uncle's bag was very heavy, so he walked (2) ________ than me. I waited for him at the top.
We were hungry, but we didn't have (3) ________ food left. Luckily, a woman at the top sold us some noodles!
The view was amazing. I could see our whole town.

items.en: *have to* = it is necessary, a rule. *had to* = a rule in the past. *don't have to* = not necessary.
items.vi: *have to* = cần thiết, quy định. *had to* = quy định trong quá khứ. *don't have to* = không cần thiết.
example: Yesterday I *had to* walk to school.

items.en: *might* and *may* = maybe. We are not sure. *could* = maybe, or an idea.
items.vi: *might* và *may* = có lẽ, chúng ta không chắc. *could* = có lẽ, hoặc một ý kiến gợi ý.
example: We *could* make a card for Grandma.

items.en: Count it: *a few*, *few*, *many*. Can't count it: *a little*, *little*, *much*. *every* and *each* + one thing.
items.vi: Đếm được: *a few*, *few*, *many*. Không đếm được: *a little*, *little*, *much*. *every* và *each* + danh từ số ít.
example: I've got *a few* stickers. There's *a little* rice.
*Every* house in our street has a garden.

items.en: Yes sentences: *some*, *something*. Questions and 'not': *any*, *anything*. *nothing* = not anything.
items.vi: Câu khẳng định: *some*, *something*. Câu hỏi và câu phủ định: *any*, *anything*. *nothing* = không có gì.
example: I've got *some* crayons. Have you got *any*?
There isn't *anything* in the box. There's *nothing* in it.

items.en: Linking words show the order: *before*, *after*, *then*, *when*. *while* = at the same time.
items.vi: Từ nối cho biết thứ tự: *before*, *after*, *then*, *when*. *while* = cùng lúc.
example: Look left and right *before* you cross.
I read a book *while* Mum was cooking.

items.en: Compare how we do things: fast, *faster*, *the fastest*; carefully, *more carefully*; well, *better*, *the best*.
items.vi: So sánh cách làm việc: fast, *faster*, *the fastest*; carefully, *more carefully*; well, *better*, *the best*.
example: Khoa sings *the best* in our class.

check.sentence: Last week we {had to|have to|might} wait for the bus for an hour.
I'm not sure. I {might|have to|had to} go to the shop later.
Can I have {a little|a few|many} sugar, please?
Dad listened to the radio {while|after|then} he was cooking.
Please speak {more quietly|quietly|most quietly} than that. The baby is asleep.

v.q: The vet says our cat is ill. We ________ give her medicine every day.
whys: 'may' means maybe, but the vet says it is necessary.
'could' gives an idea, but the vet says it is necessary.
v.hint: Who says it? Is it a maybe or something necessary?
v.worked: The vet says so, so it is necessary: 'We have to give her medicine'.

v.q: Yesterday was my sister's birthday, so I ________ buy her a present.
whys: 'have to' is the present, but 'Yesterday' is the past.
'might' means maybe, but this happened yesterday.
v.hint: Look for the time word at the start.
v.worked: 'Yesterday' is the past, so: 'I had to buy her a present'.

v.q: There's only ________ rice left. Let's buy some more.
whys: 'a few' goes with things we can count, but we cannot count rice.
'many' goes with things we can count, and 'only' means not a lot.
v.hint: Can you count rice?
v.worked: Rice is uncountable and there isn't a lot: 'only a little rice'.

v.q: ________ student in our class has a new pencil case.
whys: 'All' goes with a plural noun: all students.
'Many' goes with a plural noun: many students.
v.hint: Is 'student' one person or more than one?
v.worked: 'student' is singular, so: 'Every student'.

v.q: I haven't got ________ to wear for the party!
whys: After 'haven't' we use 'anything', not 'something'.
'haven't' and 'nothing' together make two 'no' words.
v.hint: Look for 'not' in the sentence.
v.worked: 'not' sentence + any: 'I haven't got anything to wear'.

v.q: Ella has got ________ biscuits. Would you like one?
whys: 'any' goes in questions and 'not' sentences. This is a yes sentence.
'nothing' can't go before a noun like 'biscuits'.
v.hint: Is this a yes sentence, a 'not' sentence or a question?
v.worked: A yes sentence uses 'some': 'Ella has got some biscuits'.

v.q: Wait for the green light ________ you cross the road.
whys: 'after' would mean you cross first, then wait. That's dangerous!
'while' means at the same time, but you wait first, then cross.
v.hint: Which do you do first: wait or cross?
v.worked: Wait first, then cross: 'Wait for the green light before you cross'.

v.q: Dad sang songs ________ he was washing the car.
whys: With 'was washing' the two things happen at the same time, so 'before' doesn't fit.
With 'was washing' the two things happen at the same time, so 'after' doesn't fit.
v.hint: Look at 'was washing'. Did the two things happen at the same time?
v.worked: At the same time = 'while': 'Dad sang songs while he was washing the car'.

v.q: Duc writes ________ than his brother. His writing is very neat.
whys: 'neatly' does not compare two people. Look for 'than'.
'most neatly' is for the top one of a group, not two people.
v.hint: Look for the word 'than'.
v.worked: 'than' compares two people: 'more neatly than his brother'.

v.q: Of all the girls in my team, Hana jumps ________.
whys: 'higher' compares two people, but here it is 'of all the girls'.
'high' doesn't compare. Look for 'Of all'.
v.hint: Look for 'Of all'. Is she the top one?
v.worked: 'Of all the girls' = the top one: 'Hana jumps the highest'.

v.q: "Do you want to come to my house on Sunday?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Sorry, I have to visit my aunt.
Yes, I came to your house last week.
Sorry, I had to visit my aunt.
whys: 'came' and 'last week' are the past, but Sunday is in the future.
'had to' is the past, but Sunday is in the future.
v.hint: Is the question about the past or the future? Check the verb in each reply.
v.worked: Sunday is in the future, so the reason must be now or future: 'I have to visit my aunt'.

v.q: "Will your grandpa come to the school show tonight?" Choose the best reply.
opts: He might. He's a bit tired.
He had to come last year.
He has to. He's very tired.
whys: This is about last year, but the question is about tonight.
Being tired is not a reason he must come. The two parts don't match.
v.hint: Does each reply answer 'tonight'? Does the reason make sense?
v.worked: He is tired, so maybe he will come, maybe not: 'He might. He's a bit tired.'

v.q: "What did you buy at the shop?" Choose the best reply.
whys: This answers a yes/no question, but the question starts with 'What'.
'No' answers a yes/no question, but a 'What' question needs the name of a thing.
v.hint: The question starts with 'What'. Can you answer it with yes or no?
v.worked: 'What did you buy?' 'Nothing. It was closed.' tells us what was bought.

v.q: "Would you like something to drink?" Choose the best reply.
opts: Yes, please. Some water would be nice.
No, thanks. I'd like some juice.
Yes, I drank some apple juice yesterday.
whys: 'No, thanks' and 'I'd like some juice' don't agree.
This is about yesterday, but the offer is for now.
v.hint: It is an offer for now. Does the reply agree with itself?
v.worked: A polite answer to an offer: 'Yes, please. Some water would be nice.'

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: 'might' means maybe, but the strong wind made it necessary.
'may' is about now or later, but this story is in the past and it was necessary.
v.hint: Read the whole sentence. Why did they stay inside?
v.worked: The wind was very strong, so it was necessary: 'we had to stay inside'.

stim.head: A story by Ella
stim.html:
The Big Storm
Last week there was a big storm in our town. The wind was very strong, so we (1) ________ stay inside all day.
Then the lights went off! Dad looked for candles, but there weren't (2) ________ in the cupboard. He found only two.
We sat together on the sofa. Mum told us funny stories (3) ________ the rain was falling outside.
The next morning the sky was blue again. I ran outside, and our old tree was still standing!

v.q: Read the story. Gap (1): choose the word.
whys: If there were many people, the museum would be busy, not quiet.
'much' goes with things we cannot count, but we can count people.
v.hint: Read to the end of the sentence. Was the museum busy or quiet?
v.worked: It was very quiet, so not many people came: 'There were few people there'.

stim.head: A story by Khoa
stim.html:
Our Visit to the City Museum
On Friday my class visited the city museum. There were (1) ________ people there, so it was very quiet and we could see everything.
We saw old clocks, toys and coins. My friend Max liked the clocks best.
At the end we went to the gift shop, but there was (2) ________ to buy. It was closed!
On the bus home, our teacher talked about our next trip. We (3) ________ go to the science museum. She isn't sure yet.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: 'much' goes with things we cannot count, but we can count candles.
'weren't a few' is not correct. After 'weren't' we use 'many'.
v.hint: Can you count candles? Read the next sentence too.
v.worked: Candles are countable and he found only two: 'there weren't many'.

stim.head: A story by Ella
stim.html:
The Big Storm
Last week there was a big storm in our town. The wind was very strong, so we (1) ________ stay inside all day.
Then the lights went off! Dad looked for candles, but there weren't (2) ________ in the cupboard. He found only two.
We sat together on the sofa. Mum told us funny stories (3) ________ the rain was falling outside.
The next morning the sky was blue again. I ran outside, and our old tree was still standing!

v.q: Read the story. Gap (2): choose the word.
whys: The shop was closed, so there wasn't a thing to buy.
We don't use 'anything' after 'there was'. We use it after 'there wasn't'.
v.hint: Read the next sentence. Could they buy a thing?
v.worked: The shop was closed: 'there was nothing to buy'.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (3): choose the word.
whys: The stories and the rain were at the same time, so 'before' doesn't fit.
The stories and the rain were at the same time, so 'after' doesn't fit.
v.hint: Look at 'was falling'. Did the two things happen at the same time?
v.worked: The rain was falling during the stories: 'Mum told us stories while the rain was falling'.

We sat together on the sofa. Mum told us funny stories (3) ________ the rain was falling outside.

v.q: Read the story. Gap (3): choose the word.
whys: 'had to' is a rule in the past, but the next trip is in the future.
'have to' means it is necessary, but the teacher isn't sure yet.
v.hint: Read the last sentence. Is the teacher sure?
v.worked: 'She isn't sure yet', so: 'We might go to the science museum'.

use a few, a little, many, much and every with the right nouns
